song.artist: Albert King With Stevie Ray Vaughan
song.title: Born Under a Bad Sign

guitar.modelsText: Gibson Flying V (Albert King) / Fender Stratocaster 'Number One' (Stevie Ray Vaughan)
guitar.evidence: Albert King's Gibson Flying V (often strung upside-down/left-handed) and SRV's battered Fender Stratocaster 'Number One' are both extremely well documented signature instruments.
guitar.notes: Both guitarists are iconic enough to name with confidence.

tone.target: worn blues lead with wah and gritty tube breakup
tone.profile: worn blues lead with wah and gritty tube breakup
tone.summary: A gritty, mid-focused blues lead tone using a Blues OD boost into a British clean/slight breakup amp model, complemented by wah and room ambience.

rig.name: Albert King With Stevie Ray Vaughan - Born Under a Bad Sign - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray hum and noise inherent in blues playing.
Provide the core gritty tube breakup and mid-hump required for classic blues lead work.

alternatives.reason: Good alternative, but Blues OD better captures the specific 'gritty' breakup tone.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the essential wah pedal effect for blues phrasing.
blocks.gap: The GP-180 lacks a dedicated Wah module. Using 'Boost' as a placeholder/filter control to simulate the sweeping action is the closest functional approximation.

blocks.purpose: Model the Tweed/Bluesbreaker-style amp character, providing natural tube saturation and warmth.

alternatives.reason: A viable alternative if UK SLP is too British sounding.

blocks.purpose: Provide a classic British cabinet sound that complements the blues tone.
blocks.gap: While US 2x12 might fit the 'small cab' clue, UK Vintage 4x12 is standard for this genre and offers better headroom control.

alternatives.reason: If a smaller physical cabinet sound is strictly required.

blocks.purpose: Slightly scoop the low end and boost the mids to enhance the 'center wah' focus.
Add subtle natural room ambience to give the tone depth without sounding digital or modern.

alternatives.reason: Less suitable; Room provides a more organic, vintage feel.

improvements.summary: Replace the current cabinet IR with one that better captures the small, vintage British cab sound associated with blues artists like Albert King.

proposals.recommendedAsset: British 1x or 2x Cab IR (e.g., Fender Tweed/Vox)
proposals.reason: The current UK Vintage 4x12 is too large and British; a smaller, vintage cab better matches the genre's small-to-mid sound.
